title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (with a canary stage) on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2000 paired episodes). The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and validation used a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; downstream validation and the permitted single repair call (guarded arm only) were the only mechanisms for paired outcome differences. Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary inferential test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered secondary descriptive summary (paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI, 10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We report the exact McNemar result as the preregistered confirmatory outcome, present the bootstrap CI as a secondary descriptive summary, explicitly label a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) as exploratory/post‑hoc (it was not specified in the frozen preregistration), and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, high baseline validity, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation for network operations promises reduced manual effort but raises safety risks: multi‑step sequencing errors, transient invariant violations, and protected‑field interference can convert plausible command sequences into harmful actions. Prior surveys and controlled studies document LLM hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that affect code and configuration generation, motivating architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures [1],[2].

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired experiment (cand‑003‑stud‑001) that isolates purely downstream validator/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Our precise research question is: when baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics), to what degree can a downstream deterministic validator plus a single allowed repair call (guarded pipeline with a canary stage) improve paired safe‑deploy outcomes compared with reusing the same initial candidate unmodified (baseline)? The design intentionally isolates downstream interventions (validation and at‑most‑one repair) so that any paired difference is attributable to those downstream mechanisms rather than to first‑pass generation differences such as prompt engineering, constrained decoding, or sampling variance.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired experiment (Npairs = 1000) with deterministic task selection from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 corpus and archived validator traces. (2) Full execution accounting and transparent reporting of model/adapter configuration including the recorded model_configuration.json temperature = null/unset and the interpretive caveat that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. (3) Artifact‑grounded confirmatory inferential reporting (exact two‑sided McNemar) together with preregistered descriptive bootstrap summaries and an explicit labeling of any post‑hoc one‑sided tests as exploratory.
sections.related_work:
LLMs and structured‑output tasks show frequent hallucinations and prompt sensitivity that reduce correctness for code and configuration generation; surveys and controlled studies document these effects and motivate validator‑centric defenses [1],[2]. Constrained decoding and schema‑aware planning reduce syntactic and executable errors in several structured domains, though many demonstrations derive from non‑NetOps domains and thus depend on validator fidelity when transferred to networking [3]. Recent NetOps and agentic‑AI system papers emphasize verifier‑assisted repair, guarded architectures, and protocol/proof‑carrying proposals to mitigate automation risks; these works provide prototypes and argue that operational reliability depends on validator coverage and externally enforced execution policies rather than on any single model alone [4],[5],[6].

Our study complements these works by preregistering a paired comparison whose estimand isolates the incremental effect of deterministic downstream validation and a single limited repair call when the initial candidate is held constant across conditions. That isolation avoids conflating downstream safeguards with first‑pass prompt/decoding or sampling differences and clarifies the limits of validator/repair layers under tightly controlled conditions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design. The study preregistration (cand‑003‑stud‑001) was finalized and frozen prior to any hosted‑model invocation; the preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in the execution manifest is ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec. Key preregistered elements: confirmatory paired binary design; task_count = 1000 deterministic tasks drawn from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per pair deterministically reused by both conditions); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar. Secondary preregistered summaries: paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) and sensitivity analyses treating failed calls as unsafe.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and interpretive consequences. Because both baseline and guarded episodes begin from the same sampled initial candidate, paired outcome differences can only arise from deterministic validator decisions and the permitted single repair call. This design therefore isolates downstream effects and does not measure first‑pass generation interventions (e.g., constrained decoding or independent prompt arms) that were not executed under the preregistration.

Model/runtime configuration and temperature caveat. The declared provider/model in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator version 5.0). The deterministic validator enforces workflow policies, required command presence and order, protected‑field noninterference, and emits a binary safe‑deploy verdict per task manifest.

Task corpus, selection rule, and validator semantics. Tasks were selected deterministically using the preregistered ordinal rule producing exactly 1000 unique tasks. Each task manifest contains initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty labels (very_hard, extreme). The deterministic_netops_validator_v5 compares parsed candidate command sequences against the manifest constraints in a deterministic digital‑twin emulator and emits structured validator traces archived per episode. Scoring used scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation producing the binary validity outcome used in the paired analysis.

Execution accounting and missingness. The preregistration limited retries (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1) and prespecified missingness treatments. The execution manifest records completed_episode_count = 2000, failed_episode_count = 0, hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005, and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation = 1000, repair = 5}. The primary analysis used the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' treatment; sensitivity analyses treating failures as unsafe were preregistered but unnecessary because failed episodes = 0.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting (artifact‑grounded). The run completed all planned episodes (2000) producing 1000 complete pairs with zero failed episodes. Provider audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005 and stage_counts indicating exactly 1000 shared initial generations and 5 repair calls; all deterministic consistency checks passed.

Primary paired outcomes and preregistered inferential test. The 2×2 contingency table is n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered primary confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625; this does not meet the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05 threshold, so the preregistered H1 is not supported.

Preregistered secondary descriptive summaries and sensitivity. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) yields [0.001, 0.01]. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred; representative validator traces show repairs correcting required_sequence or protected‑field violations before acceptance. Contamination checks and exclusion rules flagged no prompt‑leakage or emulator errors; no post‑hoc exclusions were applied.

Confirmatory hierarchy and bootstrap nuance (requested clarification). The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar is the confirmatory analysis and it did not reach two‑sided α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap CI and the one‑sided McNemar (computed post‑hoc as p = 0.03125) are descriptive/exploratory and do not overturn the preregistered confirmatory null. The bootstrap CI can exclude zero in this regime because percentile bootstrap summaries with 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729) applied to extremely sparse discordant counts (n10=5, n01=0) are sensitive to resampling discreteness; that sensitivity is why the bootstrap summary was preregistered as descriptive only.
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory vs descriptive outcomes and preregistration fidelity. The preregistered primary inference is the exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625), so H1 is not supported at two‑sided α = 0.05. The paired bootstrap CI ([0.001, 0.01]) is a preregistered descriptive summary and excludes zero because bootstrap sensitivity with extremely sparse discordant pairs can produce nonzero percentile bounds; this descriptive statistic does not overturn the preregistered confirmatory result. The one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in cand‑003‑stud‑001.

Power assumption mismatch and interpretive consequences. The preregistered power plan assumed baseline ≈ 0.60 and targeted an absolute increase of 0.15 to achieve >80% power at two‑sided α = 0.05. The observed baseline success rate (0.995) is far higher than that assumption; this mismatch substantially reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains because near‑unity baseline rates produce very few discordant pairs. Consequently, the study is underpowered for tiny absolute improvements in this observed regime and absence of two‑sided significance should be interpreted in that context.

Mechanistic implications within shared_initial_candidate semantics. Under the shared_initial_candidate design, only downstream validation and permitted repairs can create paired differences. The five observed repairs demonstrate that a validator with suitable coverage can correct particular ordering/sequence violations. However, the low repair invocation count may reflect few initial candidate violations in the synthetic corpus, generator behavior for the chosen model+prompt producing valid candidates, or validator coverage that does not capture other semantic error classes. Distinguishing among these mechanisms requires preregistered follow‑ups that vary generator semantics, repair budget, and validator rule sets.

Threats to validity. Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 rule coverage; omitted policy checks would inflate measured success. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate downstream effects but preclude measuring prompt/decoding interventions. External validity: the synthetic task corpus and single model (gpt‑5‑mini) limit generalization to heterogeneous production environments and other model families. Conclusion validity: extreme baseline success yields sparse discordant counts, reducing power for exact paired tests.

Operational implications and recommended follow‑ups. Artifact‑grounded evidence shows verifier‑guided repair can avert some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflow settings, but measurable marginal gains depend on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity/coverage, and permitted repair budget. Preregistered follow‑ups we recommend: (1) evaluate independent first‑pass generation arms (no shared_initial_candidate) to measure prompt/decoding intervention effects; (2) sweep repair budgets to quantify marginal returns per failure class; (3) expand validator rule suites and topology heterogeneity; and (4) include multiple model families to map model dependence. Each follow‑up should include power calculations aligned to plausible baseline failure rates and preregistered analysis choices.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total model calls used = 1005. The primary inferential outcome is the preregistered exact McNemar result; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration. These artifact‑grounded results indicate that downstream verifier/repair safeguards can prevent some unsafe outcomes, but measurable marginal gains are constrained when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the paired design isolates downstream effects. Full preregistration, execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived with the run to support reproducibility and to guide preregistered follow‑ups that broaden model diversity, validator coverage, and repair budgets.

disclosure_statement: Declared model and provider: gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). Orchestration and validator: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Preregistration: cand‑003‑stud‑001 (frozen prior to any model calls; preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in the execution manifest = ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec). Immutable initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The execution, analysis, and manuscript drafting reported here (literature review, preregistration finalization, execution, analysis, peer review and revision) were performed by the autonomous research run after the autonomy lock; no human manually edited the manuscript's technical content after that lock.
limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch is reported explicitly and reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
